title: Perception
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Perception.

concepts.def: Detection of stimuli by sensory receptors, distinct from interpretation by the brain.
The brain's interpretation and organisation of sensory information to give it meaning.
Bottom-up theory arguing perception comes directly from optic flow patterns in the environment.
Top-down theory that perception is built using prior knowledge and inference from sensory data.
Cues requiring only one eye: linear perspective, height in plane, occlusion, relative size.
Perceptual error where stimulus is misinterpreted, e.g. Muller-Lyer, Ponzo, Necker cube.

Perception — a core area of GCSE Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Perception brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Perception.
